content.text: A refund question: I'll load the refund policy.

content.content:
Use this policy for every question about refunds, returns and replacements.

1. Read the ticket first with lookup_ticket. The ticket names the order id, the
   delivery date, the items and what the customer reports. Never decide from the
   customer's message alone: dates and amounts come from the ticket.
2. The return window is 30 days from the delivery date for customers in the EU
   and 14 days everywhere else. Count calendar days. An order without a delivery
   date has not been delivered: it is a shipping problem, not a refund; say that
   the order is still on its way and that support will follow up.
3. Inside the window, an item that arrived damaged or does not work qualifies for
   a full refund or a replacement, as the customer prefers. An item the customer
   simply does not want qualifies for a refund minus the return shipping cost,
   and only when it is unused and in its original packaging.
4. Outside the window, nothing qualifies automatically. Explain the window
   politely, and say that a support manager will look at the case; do not ask
   billing.
5. Before you tell the customer a refund will be paid out, ask billing with
   ask_billing, giving the order id, the amount and the reason in one sentence.
   Only billing approves payouts. If billing does not answer, or answers with an
   error, tell the customer that the refund is approved by support and that
   billing will confirm the payout by email within two working days.
6. Gift cards, vouchers and shipping fees for orders that were delivered are
   never refunded. Digital items are refunded only when they could not be
   downloaded at all.
7. Never ask for card numbers, bank details or passwords. If the customer sends
   them, do not repeat them; tell them that support never needs them.
8. One refund per order. When the ticket shows an earlier refund for the same
   order, explain that the order was already refunded and give the date.
9. Record the outcome in one line at the end of your answer, in the form
   "Outcome: <refund | replacement | refused | manager review | shipping issue>".

When the policy does not cover a case, say so, and hand the case to a support
manager instead of guessing.
